triggers: No numeric triggers in sources; fruits Jun-Oct, under favourable weather to Dec (de.wikipedia). Weather only said to influence appearance.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Wikipedia names spruce and beech as main partners; catalogue 'broadleaf and conifer' is correct but generic. No elevation data found (catalogue 200-1600 unverified). Abundance is from Germany/Europe-wide statements.

triggers: No triggers stated. Sources say Aug-Oct (some Nov) late-season; tintling.com and pilzmuseum.at give May-Oct with autumn the main period.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Months broadly agree (catalogue Aug-Nov). Sources describe beech (also oak-hornbeam) litter on base-rich soil, a calcicole indicator. Rare in high southern Germany; no elevation range found (catalogue 200-1000 unverified). en.wikipedia lists Romania in range.

triggers: No triggers stated. Fruits on wood of any decay stage; late Apr/May to Nov, practically year-round in Germany (tintling.com).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season matches catalogue. Sources name broadleaf wood (maple, birch, beech, oak) mainly, rarely conifers, though tintling.com says beech and spruce. No elevation data (catalogue 100-1500 unverified). Abundance from Germany/Central Europe.

triggers: No triggers stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources give May-Nov; catalogue starts in June. No elevation data (catalogue 200-1800 unverified). Described as one of the most common fungi in Europe.

triggers: No triggers stated. Jul-Oct per de.wikipedia (rarely in spring); Jun-Oct per pilzlexikon.eu.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources: broadleaf trees, esp. beech (also oak-hornbeam forest, parks); pilzlexikon says both broadleaf and conifer partners but names no genera. Season Jun/Jul-Oct, catalogue Jul-Oct. Elevation not found.

triggers: No weather triggers stated. Weak parasite of old living oaks; bark injuries are entry points. Fruits Jul-Oct/Nov.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Hosts and months match. Sources: thermophilic oak-hornbeam forest, preferably calcareous, collinar to submontane; 'nirgends haeufig'/rare. Catalogue 100-800 m not numerically confirmed.

triggers: No numeric triggers. Late season; continues into December in frost-free periods (pilz-baden.ch). Forms fairy rings.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season matches. Sources: humus-rich beech forests, spruce plantations, oak-hornbeam, fresh to moderately moist soils; very common. No elevation data (catalogue 200-1500 unverified).

triggers: No triggers stated; grows on dung, old manure heaps and fertilised meadows.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season May-Oct matches. en.wikipedia says year-round in warm climates (N. America). No elevation data (catalogue 200-1800 unverified).

triggers: No triggers stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: de.wikipedia: Aug-Oct, mainly deciduous (base-rich beech) forest, rarely mixed; other sources say summer-autumn and conifer/mixed forest. Catalogue Jul-Oct and 'broadleaf and conifer' only partly supported. Elevation not found.

triggers: No numeric triggers; dung and manured pasture, esp. subalpine pastures (Almwiesen).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources: May-Nov (de.wikipedia) vs (Jun)Sep-Oct (pilzfreun.de); catalogue May-Oct. Mostly subalpine pastures, rare at intermediate elevation, 'nicht haeufig'; catalogue 100-2000 m not confirmed.

triggers: Fruits in warm spells in summer/early autumn (en.wikipedia); heat-loving, increasing with warming (de.wikipedia). No numbers.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue habitat G (grass/parks) not supported; sources say broadleaf forest. de.wikipedia: needs lime-rich soil; en.wikipedia: both calcareous and acidic soils (disagreement). Parks not mentioned. Catalogue 100-700 m unconfirmed.

triggers: No triggers stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue host Populus tremula: de.wikipedia ties aspen strictly to L. leucopodium, so aspen is likely a different taxon. en.wikipedia: poplar traditionally, plus oak and other broadleaves. pilzlexikon covers L. quercinum (oak), so it is only indirect support. Taxonomy unsettled.

triggers: No triggers stated. Late Aug-Oct, occasionally earlier or to Nov.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Host and season match. de.wikipedia: avoids strongly calcareous soil, locally common mainly in mid and high mountains, rare in lowlands; much less frequent in planted larch. Catalogue 600-1600 m consistent but no numbers found.

triggers: No numeric triggers; needs consistently wet, mossy sites (awl.ch). Aug-Nov, late summer and autumn.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Matches catalogue on hosts, wet mossy calcareous sites and season. awl.ch: mountain conifer forests, locally frequent, declining; en.wikipedia pine near seashore. Numeric elevation not found.

triggers: No triggers stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Acid soil and Betula/Picea confirmed. Sources also list pine and beech (oak only in one). Season Jun-Oct (de.wikipedia) vs Jul-Oct (pilzmuseum). Nutrient-poor moist acid soils incl. moorland; elevation not found.

triggers: No triggers stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources: Jun-Oct (catalogue Jul-Oct). de.wikipedia: mainly needle litter in old spruce forest, soils basic to neutral; fungiversum also light broadleaf woods and parks. Scattered in uplands, frequent in S. Germany, rare in N.

triggers: No triggers stated. Warmth-loving submediterranean species on south-exposed calcareous beech and oak forests.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Hosts match. Sources stress calcareous soil and very rare status (RL2 Germany; D in later list); catalogue gives no soil. Season not documented (one find 31 Jul-13 Aug), so months left null. Elevation not found.

triggers: No triggers stated. Avoids waterlogged, nitrogen-rich and heavily shaded sites; likes open pine edges.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Pinus-only host confirmed. Sources: Aug-Oct, mainly Sep-Oct (catalogue Jul-Nov is wider). de.wikipedia: soils acid to alkaline, often shallow over limestone. Spruce-bound L. deterrimus is distinct, so beware misidentification in Romania.

triggers: No numeric triggers. Fruits around St George's Day (23 Apr) in UK, March in Italy, May in Germany; later in cooler areas (en.wikipedia). Moderately moist soil with fresh grass.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season Apr-Jun matches. Saprotroph, no host: association with Crataegus/Prunus spinosa is not stated by sources. Includes forest, floodplain, parks and roadsides, not only grassland. en.wikipedia notes Romania as a major commercial source.

triggers: No triggers stated. Described as summer to autumn; one dated find 17 Nov.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources: mainly Scots pine, spruce only occasionally (catalogue lists Picea first). 'Sehr selten', RL3 Germany, VU Switzerland, so rarer than the catalogue implies. Sandy nutrient-poor soils; months and elevation not given.

triggers: No triggers stated; also fruits on buried wood and wood chips.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Mostly conifer wood, broadleaf only rarely (though expanding to wood chips and beech logs), unlike 'conifer and broadleaf'. Season differs by source: Sep-Nov, May-Dec, summer-autumn. Elevation not found.

triggers: No numeric triggers. Aug until the first hard frost in Nov (pilzbuch-pilzwelten); other sources give early summer to late autumn.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources disagree on hosts: en.wikipedia beech in Europe, pilzbuch conifers (spruce, fir, pine). Quercus is not supported for Europe. Season broader (Jun-Dec) than main Aug-Nov. Elevation not found.

triggers: No triggers stated. Unfertilised short-grass sites; declining with grassland intensification.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources: Jun-Nov (catalogue Jul-Nov); also semi-dry and steppe grassland, orchards, parks, forest clearings. de.wikipedia mentions calcareous sites; awl.ch says nutrient-poor, fresh to moist. Elevation 200-2000 unconfirmed.

triggers: No triggers stated; late May to early Jul. Elevation: Germany, 'in tiefen Lagen, selten ueber 500 m' (lower bound not stated).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue habitat G is partly wrong: sources say broadleaf forest, parks, shrubland. Quercus not named by sources. Elevation rarely above 500 m vs catalogue 100-900. Months and calcareous soil confirmed.

triggers: No triggers stated; moist sandy-grassy spots.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources give Jun-Sep (pilzfinder) or summer-autumn (catalogue Jul-Oct). 'Sehr selten' in 123pilzsuche. Habitat parks, gardens, mixed forest paths and clearings. Elevation not found. Only two thin sources.

triggers: No triggers stated; spring fruiting Apr-May only.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources: Apr-May (catalogue Mar-May). Catalogue habitat W is wrong: floodplains, stream valleys, hedges, meadows, forest edges. Crataegus/Rosaceae link not stated. Sources call it a soil saprobe; rare, NT in Switzerland. Elevation not found.

triggers: Fruiting follows snowmelt (fungiversum). Winter-early spring; no numeric triggers.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season conflict: Jan-May (fungiversum) vs Dec-Mar (pilze-vorarlberg); Jan-Mar is the overlap, catalogue has Jan-Apr. Frequent in Alpine/pre-Alpine areas, rarely in lowlands; catalogue 100-1200 m not matched. Mainly alder and willow twigs.

triggers: No triggers stated; appears from July, peaking in autumn (pilzmuseum).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Fagus supported (wnsinfo); sources say only 'conifer forests' with no genus, so Abies/Picea unconfirmed. Base-rich/calcareous soils; found mainly at higher elevations, otherwise rare (consistent with 400-1500 m, no numbers).

triggers: No triggers stated; fruits relatively early (May-Aug).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue 'acid warm' contradicted: de.wikipedia says lime-rich soil. Season May-Aug vs catalogue Jul-Sep. Fagus unsupported; mycopedia lists only Quercus ilex, flagged uncertain ('cf'). Rare. Elevation not found.

triggers: No triggers stated; late June to November.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Strict beech companion, confirmed. Months Jun-Nov (de.wikipedia) vs Aug-Oct. Elevation: lowland to 1050 m Black Forest, 1600 m Apennines, 1800 m Swiss Alps (catalogue 300-1300 too narrow). No pH demands; among most frequent milk caps with beech in DE/AT/CH.

triggers: No triggers stated; clustered on stumps and roots, also buried wood.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources: almost exclusively hardwood (conifers very rare), unlike 'broadleaf and conifer'. natur-in-nrw: avoids elevation, prefers below 500 m (Germany), vs catalogue 100-1200. Also weak parasite on living hardwood roots. Season summer to late autumn.

triggers: No triggers stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Hosts (willow, alder, beech) and floodplain habitat confirmed. Season Aug-Oct (fungiversum) vs May-Dec (fundkorb); catalogue Jun-Oct. 'Not particularly common'. Elevation 200-1000 unconfirmed.
